title: ISO/IEC 27005 Lead Risk Manager
summary: The ISO/IEC 27005 Lead Risk Manager is a professional certification for people who run information security risk management rather than merely take part in it. It is built on the guidance in ISO/IEC 27005 and is delivered by accredited training bodies, so the standard is exam code 27005 rather than a vendor exam number. The level sits between practitioner and manager: candidates are expected to know the vocabulary of risk, to apply a repeatable method, and to explain their decisions to auditors and executives. The exam is normally a written paper of multiple choice and scenario questions, and some providers add a practical assignment based on a case study. It suits security analysts, risk officers, auditors and consultants who already work with ISO/IEC 27001 and now need the deeper risk skills. Typical next roles are information security risk manager, governance risk and compliance manager, and security consultant. The domain list below follows the published structure used by training providers, so check the current version with your provider before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not endorsed by any standards body or training provider.

beginner.definition: This is a professional certificate about information security risk management, based on a published international standard, ISO 27005. Risk management means deciding what could go wrong, how likely it is and how much harm it would cause. The lead part means you learn to guide the whole process, not just fill in a form.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every company has more weaknesses than time or money to fix. Risk management is the skill of choosing the work that matters most. This certificate proves you can make those choices in a way that auditors and managers accept. It fits analysts, auditors and security officers who want to move into governance and risk roles. It also pairs well with ISO 27001, because risk assessment sits at the heart of that standard.
howItWorks: Learn the shared vocabulary first, including asset, threat, vulnerability, likelihood, impact and risk owner.
Study one complete risk method from start to finish, so you can see how the steps connect.
Practise on a small case study and write a short risk register with a score for each entry.
Compare treatment options such as reducing, avoiding, sharing and accepting a risk, and justify each choice.
Ask a colleague to challenge your ratings, because exam scenario questions often test whether your reasoning holds.
Sit the exam, which mixes definition questions with case study questions about a risk programme.
beginner.example: Imagine you are planning a long car journey with your family. You look at the weather, the age of the tyres and the length of the drive. You decide some risks are worth taking and you reduce the others. So you buy new tyres and skip the mountain road. You also accept the risk of a short delay. Nobody stops every possible accident, but a careful driver reduces the worst ones. Security risk management works in exactly the same way.
takeaways: Risk work is about choosing what not to fix as much as choosing what to fix.
You must be able to explain the reason behind every score you write down.
Check your provider's current exam and assignment format before you book a date.

objectives: Explain the concepts, terms and principles that information security risk management uses
Establish context and scope so that risk decisions match the organisation and its obligations
Identify, analyse and evaluate risk with a method that another person could repeat
Select and document risk treatment options, including the acceptance of residual risk
Describe how risk is communicated to owners, executives and other interested parties
Monitor, review and improve a risk management process over time

chapters.title: Concepts and definitions of information security risk
objectives: Define asset, threat, vulnerability, incident, likelihood, consequence and risk in your own words
Explain how risk differs from a weakness or a control gap in everyday security language
Apply the risk management principles set out in the wider ISO 27000 family of standards
Describe how information security risk relates to operational, financial and legal risk
Explain the difference between inherent risk and residual risk after controls are applied

chapters.title: Establishing context, scope and risk criteria
objectives: Define the scope of a risk assessment, including which systems, sites and processes are inside it
Document the internal and external context that shapes the organisation's tolerance for risk
Agree risk criteria and scales that decision makers understand and accept
Identify interested parties and record what each one needs from the risk process
Produce a risk assessment plan with roles, timescales and review points

chapters.title: Risk identification and analysis
objectives: Inventory the information assets and business processes that a risk assessment depends on
Identify credible threat sources and the vulnerabilities that a threat could use
Estimate likelihood and consequence and record the reasoning behind each estimate
Use qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative techniques and choose the right one for the case
Determine the level of risk by comparing results against the agreed criteria
Record findings in a risk register that can be read by a non-specialist manager

chapters.title: Risk treatment and acceptance
objectives: Choose between modifying, avoiding, sharing and retaining a risk and justify the choice
Select controls that are proportionate to the risk and check for any that already exist
Write a risk treatment plan with owners, deadlines and expected effect on the risk level
Explain how risk owners formally accept residual risk and how that decision is recorded
Describe how risk treatment options are compared when budgets are limited
Explain how risk assessment results feed a statement of applicability or control selection

chapters.title: Risk communication, monitoring and review
objectives: Build a communication approach that tells each audience what it needs to know about risk
Report risk status to executives using measures that support a decision rather than a score alone
Define the triggers that require a risk assessment to be repeated or updated
Monitor accepted risks and controls so that changes in the environment are noticed
Describe how lessons from incidents and audits are fed back into the risk process

chapters.title: Risk management methods and continual improvement
objectives: Compare common risk assessment methods and explain when each approach is useful
Explain how a risk management process is embedded into an existing management system
Identify the records and evidence an auditor will expect to see for a risk assessment
Describe how the whole risk process is reviewed and improved over successive cycles
